text:
maria: @anya heads-up from sales — AcmeHealth wants a VPC + on-prem package. They need data-residency in eu-west-1, FIPS KMS, and an offline install option. Customer asked: feasible timeline and blockers? :eyes:
anya: thanks, Maria. Do we have the full requirements doc or just the sales notes? what's their size/throughput expectations?
maria: just the sales intake so far, pasted key asks here: 'VPC peering or direct connect, private control plane, HSM/KMS integration (FIPS), no internet egress, support for RHEL8 & 9, GPU nodes w/ driver management, audit logs retention 7 years.'
kevin: rough dependency checklist from SE side — quick list first, details after:
```
- Network: Direct Connect or Transit Gateway + routing, DNS for private control plane
- Auth: customer KMS/HSM integration, service-account mapping
- Storage: NFS or Ceph for model artifacts, snapshot backup plan
- Images: air-gapped install images, signed artifacts
- Drivers: NVIDIA drivers + CUDA matrix, DKMS or pinned images
- OS: RHEL8/9 support + kernel compat tests
- Entitlements: licensing + offline activation process
- Observability: push logs to customer SIEM or S3 (on-prem)
- Rollout: canary -> full, with fallback to hosted model
```
kevin: estimate 6-10 weeks for an air-gapped installer + validated matrix (OS x GPU x driver) if we reuse our Dedicated infra configs. If we need custom on-prem packaging for AcmeHealth's peculiar PKI, add 2-3 weeks.
sam: +1 on timeline. Add infra tasks: validated Terraform modules for their VPC layout, a hardened kubeadm or k8s operator path, and a smoke test harness that runs locally. Also need a security review and legal sign-off for data residency.
anya: priority/next steps from product POV: 1) capture exact SLA request and throughput numbers; 2) confirm KMS/HSM vendor and whether customer will provide HSM or wants Redwood to integrate with their cloud KMS; 3) intake into backlog as candidate P1 for enterprise; 4) define launch criteria (install test pass, perf within 10% of hosted baseline, audit logs export).
maria: I can loop in the Acme AE and ask for KMS vendor + perf numbers. I'll attach the support ticket: #ACME-987 to this thread. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Ticket created: ACME-987 (private-deploy request) — link: https://redwood.support/tickets/ACME-987
kevin: from a risky-dependency view: HSM vendors (Thales/Entrust) have slow cert workflows; network egress restrictions often break runtime updates (we need a secure package mirror). Recommend we offer 2 delivery options: (A) managed private control plane with peered network (faster), (B) full air-gapped on-prem bundle (longer timeline, higher price).
anya: agree. For backlog intake, I'll create a MRD and an epic with two tracks (managed-vpc, airgap). Can someone add acceptance criteria? I'll list: install success, model inference smoke tests, end-to-end latency under threshold (configurable), and KMS key rotation tested.
sam: acceptance tests I'd add: automated vulnerability scan of images, recovery/restore test of model artifacts, and a simulated network partition test.
kevin: also doc the rollback path: if customer reports perf regression, we need a quick switch to a hosted variant or config toggle. Add a feature-flag path to allow remote fallback (with customer consent).
maria: timeline ask from Acme: 'production within Q3'. They asked for a proposal by EOW. Is that realistic? :calendar:
anya: EOW proposal is OK — we can give a proposed plan + rough timeline and list of blocking items. But we should mark the epic as 'needs-eng-commit' and not promise dates until SE/infra ack.
kevin: I'll draft a technical feasibility note with the dependency matrix and pandas-style testing matrix by Tue.
sam: I'll scope the Terraform and smoke tests, and put a PR with a draft test harness.
maria: great — I'll tell Acme we'll deliver a proposal by Friday and that dates are tentative pending engineering sign-off.
anya: assigning owners: @kevin (tech note + dependency matrix), @sam (infra tests + terraform modules), @maria (customer liaison + requirements). I'll create the epic and link ACME-987.
maria: thanks everyone. :wave:
